(a) The decisive text is not the mailing list but E73 Information Object's scope note: 'An instance of E73 Information Object does not depend on a specific physical carrier, which can include human memory' -- since E29 IS-A E73, an undocumented technique carried in the miller's memory is admitted by the standard itself, which makes Stead's t0761 message a gloss rather than the sole basis. (b) Neither answer confronts the one clause in the standard that cuts the other way: P33's scope note distinguishes it from P32 because the E29 is 'a concrete information object in its own right rather than simply being a term or a method known by tradition'. It survives here only because the case stresses the technique is personal and unlike the predecessor's, i.e. not traditional -- but that is the constraint an adversarial reading turns on and both missed it. (c) t0761's own thread resolves onto the technique/feature pair (Oldman's P56 bears feature -> E25 Human-Made Feature; the 'Grammaticus' reply distinguishing E29-as-procedure from E29-as-schema-of-the-expected-product). Documenting the groove pattern as an E25 Human-Made Feature borne by the millstone via P56 is what actually lets the museum answer 'has it always ground the same way' from surviving evidence rather than from assertion.
